quickSummary: The eukaryotic cell cycle comprises Interphase (95% duration: G1, S, G2) and M-Phase. Mature non-dividing cells exit G1 into the metabolically active G0 quiescent state. G1 involves active RNA and protein synthesis (2n, 2C). In S-phase, nuclear DNA doubles (2C -> 4C) while chromosome count remains strictly constant (2n), and the cytoplasmic centriole pair duplicates. G2 synthesizes tubulin and prepares the cell for mitotic entry (2n, 4C).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1. The Eukaryotic Cell Cycle Framework
conceptBreakdown.title: 1. The Eukaryotic Cell Cycle Framework

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Interphase represents 95% of cell cycle time. In S-phase, DNA doubles from 2C to 4C while chromosome number remains constant (2n).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
THE EUKARYOTIC CELL CYCLE
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
   INTERPHASE (95% Duration)                                  M-PHASE (Mitotic Phase)
(Preparatory Growth & DNA Replication)                     (Nuclear & Cytoplasmic Division)
 ├── G₁ Phase (Gap 1 - Cell Growth)                         ├── Karyokinesis (Pro/Meta/Ana/Telo)
 ├── S Phase (Synthesis - DNA Replication)                  └── Cytokinesis (Cell Cleavage)
 └── G₂ Phase (Gap 2 - Protein Synthesis)
conceptBreakdown.content:
The **Cell Cycle** is an ordered, genetically coordinated sequence of events whereby a cell duplicates its genome, synthesizes its structural constituents, and divides into two daughter cells.

### Temporal Variations
• **Cultured Human Cells**: $\approx 24\text{ hours}$ ($G_1 \approx 10\text{ h}, S \approx 8\text{ h}, G_2 \approx 4\text{ h}, M \approx 1\text{ h}$).
• **Budding Yeast (*Saccharomyces cerevisiae*)**: $\approx 90\text{ minutes}$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.1 The Quiescent State ($G_0$ Phase)
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.1 The Quiescent State ($G_0$ Phase)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Mature differentiated cells in adult animals that do not undergo division (such as **cardiac myocytes** and **mature neurons**) exit the $G_1$ phase into an inactive metabolic state termed the **$G_0$ Phase (Quiescent Stage)**.
• Cells in $G_0$ remain **metabolically active and functionally differentiated**, but no longer proliferate unless stimulated by specific mitogenic growth factors (*e.g., liver parenchymal cells during tissue injury and regeneration*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Interphase Molecular Sub-Stages
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Interphase Molecular Sub-Stages
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
INTERPHASE MOLECULAR EVENTS
                          
   G₁ PHASE ──────────────► High RNA & Protein Synthesis; Organelle Duplication
                            (2n Chromosomes, 2C DNA Content)
                                       │
   S PHASE ───────────────► **DNA REPLICATION** (Nuclear) + **CENTRIOLE DUPLICATION** (Cytoplasm)
                            (2n Chromosomes, 4C DNA Content)
                                       │
   G₂ PHASE ──────────────► Tubulin Synthesis; Preparation for Mitosis
                            (2n Chromosomes, 4C DNA Content)
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **$G_1$ Phase (Gap 1 / Post-Mitotic Phase)**: High synthesis of mRNA, non-histone proteins, nucleotides, and ATP. Mitochondria and other organelles duplicate ($2n, 2C$).
2. **$S$ Phase (Synthesis Phase)**:
   $$\Large \mathbf{\text{DNA Content: } 2C \longrightarrow 4C}$$
   $$\Large \mathbf{\text{Chromosome Number: } 2n \longrightarrow 2n \text{ (UNCHANGED)}}$$
   - **Nuclear Event**: Semi-conservative DNA replication; synthesis of basic histone proteins.
   - **Cytoplasmic Event**: Duplication of the **Centrosome / Centriole Pair** in animal cells.
3. **$G_2$ Phase (Gap 2 / Pre-Mitotic Phase)**: Synthesis of $\alpha$- and $\beta$-Tubulin proteins for mitotic spindle assembly; chloroplasts and mitochondria multiply ($2n, 4C$).
